learning.title: A parsed lint summary is not the gate — the hook and CI are; grep-of-output lies about clean
learning.body:
dev-workflows hit this on #518 (2026-11-17): their own lint grep reported clean while the pre-commit hook caught a prefer-const — deno lint prints findings in a shape their grep pattern did not match. They fixed and re-ran rather than --no-verify.
Rule: when you summarize a gate's output through grep/jq/node parsing, the PARSER is now part of your gate and can silently fail to match. Trust, in order: the gate's own exit code, the hook, then CI. A parsed summary is a convenience for reporting, never evidence of clean. If a hook and your summary disagree, the hook is right until proven otherwise — and the proof is a re-run, not an argument.
The failure mode to fear: a seat trusting its own summary over the hook and pushing a red gate with a green-sounding report.
